intent_en: To explain that test-optional colleges report higher average test scores than test-required colleges because students selectively submit their higher scores, inflating the school's statistics.
previous_intent: To illustrate the trend of higher average SAT scores at test-optional colleges compared to test-required colleges and explain how student self-selection of submitted scores inflates these reported statistics.
narration_support: Second, their average test scores are higher... Students with higher scores will choose to submit them... inflating their accepted school's average statistics.
chart_support: Line chart comparing Average SAT (25% tile) for test-optional and test-required colleges from 1992 to 2010, showing test-optional averages generally exceeding test-required averages.
evidence_note: The narration explicitly states that test-optional schools have higher averages due to self-selection. The chart visualizes this by plotting the 25th percentile SAT scores for test-optional (blue) vs test-required (grey) colleges, where the test-optional line is generally higher, especially in later years.
